To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

science education is only one of the activities in which a person engages, science education is only the object/motive of one of the activities, the object/motive that science education is oriented to is not the object/motive to which science education is oriented in the classroom, and the subjectification that occurs in one activity is different from the subjectification that takes place in another activity.

science education is only one of the activities that individuals engage in, and that the diversity of activities in which individuals engage leads to a hierarchy of object/motive relations, which, in turn, leads to the formation of a personality that is unique for each individual.

(1) the object/motive of a person’s everyday activity is a collective object/motive, which is a collective object of activity, (2) the subject/motive of a particular everyday activity is a person’s motive, which is a person’s object of activity, and (3) the person is the person of a person’s motive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how individuals develop their personalities through their movement across the diverse everyday activities in which they participate.
the development of science education as a part of the development of the individual’s personality.
how individuals move across diverse everyday activities, and how they develop a hierarchy of object/motive that shapes their personality and their learning in science.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the diversity-of-life perspective provides us with a framework for understanding the development of science and science education within and across the multiple and diverse activities of the everyday life of the individual person.
we are what we do and that what we do depends on who we are.
the diversity of life in the everyday life, which is structured by activities that are oriented to diverse object/motives, is the source of diversity in science education and science.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

science education is not a separate domain of life, but rather an activity that is embedded in a larger ensemble of activities, which together constitute the life of a person, the person’s personality.
the science education that we observed in the everyday life was not a process of learning, but rather a process of subjectification.
we have found that science education is a minor activity in the life of the person, but that science education is nevertheless important for the development of the person.
The main takeaway from our work is that
science and its education cannot be understood without taking into account its role in the everyday life and personality of a person.
the diversity of life, as it is lived by each person, is the source of the diversity of science education, as it is experienced by each person.

we should think of learning not as a process that takes place inside science classrooms, but as the continual development of a hierarchy of object/motive across the diverse activities that constitute the individual’s life.
